why_lift_and_not_win_rate: Raw win rate is meaningless for cross-card comparison because the 3.33:1 TP/SL geometry and gold's 15.6-year drift generate win rate by themselves. Proof from this very table: H2 has the HIGHEST win rate of all cards at 46.17% yet nearly the LOWEST skill at 0.811pp, because its own null baseline is also the highest at 45.36%. A ranking by win rate would have chosen exactly the wrong card. Every card therefore builds its own control and only the difference is reported.
screen_caveat: The scanner uses 12 permutations per arm, so its LIFT is comparable across cards but its Z IS NOT comparable against the 3.09 or 3.328 engine bars - with 12 draws perm_sd is under-estimated and z is inflated roughly 1.7-fold (verified on M30: scanner z=2.926 vs adjudicator z=1.75 at 40 permutations). No verdict is issued from this file.

cards_structurally_impossible.mechanism: These timeframes bar the clock at intervals that never land on hour 22 or 23. H3 opens at 00/03/06/.../21, H6 at 00/06/12/18, H8 at 00/08/16, H12 at 00/12, D1 once daily, W1 weekly, MN1 monthly. The hour-22/23 hypothesis is therefore UNDEFINED on these cards, not weak.
cards_structurally_impossible.reusable_lesson: Any time-of-day layer inherits this constraint. A future AI seeing zero trades on H3 should not diagnose a data fault.

findings.1_resolution_step_change: Lift TRIPLES from the hourly cards (H1 0.690, H2 0.811) to the sub-30-minute band (1.62 to 2.27). This is genuine MECHANISTIC support for the layer's own hypothesis: 'enter at the open following the 22:00 close' resolves to one coarse moment on an hourly bar but pins entry to a narrow slice of the Asian-session open on a 5-30 minute bar, so a real session-open effect must sharpen with resolution - and it measurably does.
findings.2_saturation_with_characteristic_scale: Within M1 to M30 lift is FLAT at 1.62 to 2.27pp with no monotone trend, and the finest card M1 (1.812) is WORSE than M5 (2.270) and M30 (2.037). The effect therefore has a characteristic time scale of roughly 5 to 30 minutes and further resolution buys nothing. Going 30x finer from M30 to M1 LOWERED lift by 11%.
findings.3_filter_is_real_and_carries_most_of_the: The regime filter raises lift on EVERY one of the twelve cards, by 1.44x to 8.31x. The bare hour rule is nearly worthless on its own - 0.083pp on H1, 0.427pp on M6 - and outright NEGATIVE on H2 at -0.249pp. So roughly half to seven-eighths of all measured skill comes from the mom13 momentum filter rather than from the nightly hour. The second lever is real; the first lever alone is not a layer.
findings.4_the_negative_verdict: ALL TWELVE measured cards fall below the 4.0pp H3 lift floor. The best, M5, reaches 57% of the bar; the mean across cards is 1.708pp, i.e. 43% of the bar. There is no timeframe on which this layer's skill is sufficient, and the MTF route - the last avenue the eternal-death rule required testing - is therefore closed.
findings.5_why_win_rate_ranking_would_have_failed: H2 has the highest win rate (46.17%) and the second-lowest lift (0.811pp); M5 has a mid-table win rate (44.65%) and the highest lift (2.270pp). Ranking cards by win rate would have selected H2 - a card whose bare base arm has NEGATIVE skill. This is direct evidence for the project's rule that a control is mandatory.

capacity_notes.m1_required_two_engineering_fixes: M1 at 5,000,000 bars killed the sandbox twice. Fix 1 (step 46): sample the unconditional arm at 50,000 eligible bars instead of all of them, validated on M30 where the full answer is computable (error -0.041pp). Fix 2 (step 48): pass copy=False to the DataFrame constructor, removing a silent 228MB duplication (326MB -> 554MB became 326MB flat, np.shares_memory True). After both, M1 completes in 90.5 seconds inside a 985MB sandbox.
capacity_notes.cost_scaling: Post-fix runtimes: M30 8.1s, M10 53s, M6 21.2s, M5 25.0s, M4 31.0s, M3 41.3s, M1 90.5s. Cost is now roughly linear in bar count instead of exploding.
